The BRL-S architectures employ quantized priorities and first-in, first-out (FIFO) buckets to simplify scheduling. Three configurations with two, four, and eight priority levels are evaluated. FPGA synthesis results demonstrate that BRL-S reduces lookup-table utilization by approximately 68--72% compared with RL-S. ASIC synthesis further shows reductions of 63--67% in area and 64--69% in estimated power consumption. These results demonstrate that bucket-based scheduling substantially improves the hardware efficiency of reinforcement-learned QLDPC decoders.

title: Biharmonic submanifolds in nonpositive space forms
abstract: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. We also prove that every biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in a four-dimensional nonpositive space form is minimal. These results provide substantial support for Chen's conjecture and the generalized Chen's conjecture for hyperbolic space in higher codimensions.

title: Infinite-Horizon Stochastic Recursive Differential Games with Jumps: Nonautonomous Coefficients and Nonzero Terminal Values
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a class of decoupled infinite-horizon forward--backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) with time-dependent coefficients and jumps. Under suitable time-integrability conditions on the coefficient growth and stochastic Lipschitz moduli, we establish an $L^p$ theory ($p\ge 2$) for these systems, including well-posedness, moment estimates, conditional stability, and tail estimates, without imposing dissipativity of the forward dynamics or monotonicity of the backward generator in its value variable. In particular, the forward state converges in $L^p$ and almost surely to a limiting random variable $X_\infty$, while the backward solution converges to the generally nonzero terminal value $Φ(X_\infty)$. Within this framework, we study infinite-horizon two-player zero-sum stochastic recursive differential games. We prove that the lower and upper value functions are deterministic and establish the dynamic programming principle (DPP) using backward stochastic semigroups and nonanticipative strategies. Both value functions converge locally uniformly to $Φ$ as the initial time tends to infinity and are characterized as viscosity solutions of the corresponding non-autonomous, nonlocal Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman--Isaacs (HJBI) equations. Under an additional integrable Lyapunov-barrier condition, we establish a comparison principle for continuous viscosity subsolutions and supersolutions of uniform linear growth, provided that at least one is uniformly Lipschitz in space. This yields uniqueness for both HJBI equations in the linear-growth class. Finally, we establish a weaker, contact-wise Isaacs criterion ensuring that the lower and upper value functions coincide and hence that the game has a value.

title: Schrodinger group along the horocycles and Egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
abstract:
In this paper, we study Egorov's theorem for Laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in Zelditch's quantization. In this quantization, the remainder in Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. Forward in time, we show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the Ehrenfest time T_E=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter.
  Backward in time, we introduce the Schrodinger group along the stable horocycles, which absorbs the exponentially growing part of the remainder. We show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid up to -T_E+T_h for any Th going to infinity with 0<=T_h<=T_E. Moreover, the limit of the remainder in Egorov's theorem at the Ehrenfest time -T_E is exactly the difference between the semiclassical measure and the Liouville measure, tested against the symbols propagated by the Schrodinger group. Consequently, Egorov's theorem for a sequence of eigenfunctions holds at -T_E (and in fact, at -T_E-T for any fixed T in R if and only if the sequence tends to be equidistributed in the phase space. Thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture is equivalent to this Egorov property holding for every eigenbasis. Furthermore, QUE holds with a polynomial rate if and only if Egorov's theorem holds at -T_E with a polynomial remainder. In this case, Egorov's theorem holds beyond -T_E with a polynomial remainder, and the stronger the rate is in QUE, the longer the time is in Egorov's theorem.

title: Minimax signal detection in regression under differential privacy
abstract: We establish minimax separation rates across sparsity levels for regression signal detection under $(ε, δ)$-central differential privacy, considering linear regression with an unknown error distribution and generalised linear models (GLMs) with an unknown intercept. Without sparsity restrictions, the separation rates for linear regression and GLMs with binary responses match the private Gaussian mean testing rate up to polylogarithmic factors. For GLMs with more than two possible response outcomes, additional information in the marginal response distribution permits faster detection of sufficiently small signals when the dimension exceeds the sample size $n$. Our upper bounds are based on a reduction to private mean testing, tests of dependence between the response and sparse covariate projections, and a response-only test that is adjusted for the unknown intercept. The resulting procedure adapts to unknown sparsity and matches our lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. We also construct polynomial-time tests that attain these rates when $ε\gtrsim n^{-1/2}$, and compare their numerical performance with existing private procedures.

title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
abstract: Jaeger conjectured that, for every positive integer $p$, every $4p$-edge-connected graph admits an orientation with congruent indegree and outdegree modulo $2p+1$. We prove a stronger probabilistic counterpart: a uniformly random simple $(4p+1)$-regular graph has a strongly connected orientation with all outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$ with probability tending to one as its even order grows. More generally, for every fixed odd $d\ge9$, there is $\varepsilon_d>0$ such that its circular flow number is less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ with probability tending to one. We give explicit margins at the small degrees and prove the bound $91/33$ at degree seven, answering a fixed-upper-bound question of Li and Li. Gaps below $3$ at degree five and below $8/3$ at degree seven remain open. A uniform estimate for dense bisections also gives short intervals above the Li--Li maximum-bisection lower bound. Finally, we prove the one-unit bisection-gap conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis: at every fixed degree $d\ge3$, the typical minimum parameter for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the threshold forced by the maximum bisection by at most one.

title: How Does One Cut a 30-60-90 Triangle?
abstract: We enumerate dissections of a 30-60-90 triangle into smaller triangles similar to itself, counting unlabeled arrangements up to similarity and reflection. There are 18 four-piece, 121 five-piece, and 844 six-piece arrangements, corresponding to 11, 47, and 235 distinct multisets of piece areas. We present illustrated catalogs organized by these area multisets and distinguish layouts obtained by subdivision and local rotations or reflections from independent layouts. A separately implemented computational search reproduces every arrangement up to nine pieces, finding 460404 arrangements. Counts through nine pieces for five other classes of triangles are included for comparison.

title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
abstract:
We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum.
  We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_σ\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $σ\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

title: On Gallai $d$-colored circulants
abstract: A $d$-graph is a complete graph whose edges are colored with colors from $[d]$. It is Gallai if it contains no triangle whose three edges have distinct colors. We prove that every Gallai $d$-circulant is an iterated lexicographic product of circulants using at most two colors. The proof uses the compatibility of the known canonical modular decomposition with the cyclic action. For $d$-graphs avoiding both a rainbow triangle $Δ$ and the two-colored four-vertex graph $Π$ whose chromatic components are paths, we give a more explicit classification. Color-preserving vertex transitivity is equivalent to circular symmetry and to a reduced positional game tree whose branching numbers and labels depend only on depth. The edge colors in the given cyclic labeling are determined by a chain of divisors of the order. This description yields a complete isomorphism invariant and a linear-time recognition procedure in the difference-word representation. The characterization of CIS $d$-circulants reduces to CIS two-colored factors. Finally, we extend the numerical CIS criterion to $d$-graphs whose chromatic components are vertex-transitive.

title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every bijective non-contractive self-map has the following structure: the quasi-metric splits as $d = λ^- + D_0$. The invariant limit register $λ^-$ is a quasi-pseudo-metric below $d$ for which the map is an isometry, with totally bounded symmetrization on every orbit, so that the map's rigid shadow is a rotation of a compact monothetic group; the asymmetric limit structure on it, a priori only paratopological, carries the compact topology. The defect $D_0$ lies in a band between a past fee difference and the fee of its source, the fee nondecreasing along orbits and vanishing in the deep past. The defect is zero precisely when the map is an isometry. Deep sources are thus almost rigid: in the deep past the map is an isometry to within any $\varepsilon$, against every target. Every such map that is not an isometry is a toll over its rigid shadow, levied on a forward-invariant zone that sheds into the past. Two further facts are forced: the orbit of the source of any strict pair is infinite and already strict, and the source pays its whole defect on its own backward returns, uniformly on a chain-closed set of displacements. The band is attained at both ends, and beyond it the shape of the defect is not forced: three spirals over the circle show that the toll can depend on the target, that a source carrying a fee can descend for free, and that an ascent can carry defect; no rate of shedding is forced either, and for zone tolls (two-valued descent tolls that are shift-monotone and subadditive along their own routes) the fee reaches zero already at a finite depth, by the ascending chain condition on submonoids of $\mathbb{N}$. The results are machine-checked in Lean, apart from a few statements listed at the end.

title: Optimal Subsidy Design for Productive Investment across Markets
abstract: We study the optimal design of investment subsidies across heterogeneous monopolistic markets subject to a common expected discounted budget. Each producer faces a regular one-dimensional demand diffusion and chooses irreversible capacity expansion through a singular stochastic control problem. The regulator values weighted consumer surplus, producer profits, and an additional benefit from installed capacity, while accounting for the excess cost of raising public funds. We characterize producers' optimal investment responses through free boundaries and reformulate the regulator's stochastic optimization problem as a deterministic optimization over investment boundaries. An integral representation then recovers the optimal subsidy schedules that implement the resulting capacity policies. Under mild conditions on the diffusions, we establish existence of optimal schedules and uniqueness of the induced investment policies. Finally, we characterize the subsidy schedule and provide numerical illustrations.

title: A transition calculus for 0-pseudodifferential operators with applications to gas giant geometry
abstract: A gas giant Riemannian metric $g$ on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold-with-boundary $M$ blows up at the boundary $\partial M$ at the rate $1/x^α$, for $α\in (0,2)$, where $x \in C^\infty(M)$ is a boundary-defining function. Such metrics arise in the modeling of acoustic waves in gaseous planets. De Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykkänen-Mazzeo [arXiv:2403.05475] showed that, if $α> 2/n$, the Laplace-Beltrami operator $Δ_g$ is essentially self-adjoint and has discrete spectrum. Moreover, its spectrum is stable under truncations of $M$. The proof leverages the 0-calculus of Mazzeo-Melrose. We extend this theory by introducing a 0-transition calculus for studying families of 0-operators. We demonstrate a parametrix construction for $Δ_g$ that is stable under truncations. Using this, we study the behavior of the resolvent of $Δ_g$ under truncation and extend the characterization of the spectrum obtained by de Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykkänen-Mazzeo. In particular, we prove that (on appropriate functional-analytic domains) simple eigenvalues admit asymptotic expansions in the truncation parameter $ε$ and that the corresponding eigenfunctions admit joint asymptotic expansions in $(ε, x)$.

title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

title: Higher zeroes in pointed infinity-categories
abstract: We construct an endofunctor on (small) simplicial sets which freely adjoins a zero object to a (small) infinity-category, as the co-cone construction freely adjoins a terminal object. We then prove that this endofunctor induces a left adjoint to the inclusion of the infinity-category of (small) pointed infinity-categories and morphisms that preserve zero objects into the infinity-category of (small) infinity-categories. This adjunction, in turn, leads to the definition of a coherent choice of nullhomotopies on a pointed infinity-category. A coherent choice of nullhomotopies is a non-canonical, coherent choice of "higher zeroes" on a pointed infinity-category, mirroring the obvious definition of higher zeroes on the differential graded nerve of a differential graded category of chain complexes over an additive category. We then show that coherent choices of nullhomotopies give an alternate characterization of fiber sequences in pointed infinity-categories, generalizing the 1-categorical definition of kernels in terms of morphisms that compose to zero.

title: The Arc Threshold of the Two-Row Ising Torus: Exact Factorization, an Algebraic Critical Coupling, Uniformity in the Circumference, and the Rate of Convergence
abstract: The Lee-Yang circle theorem places every zero of a ferromagnetic Ising partition polynomial on the unit circle. The arc condition, that every zero lie in the closed left half-plane, turns the circle theorem into a product formula for the characteristic function of the occupation count and makes it usable for local limit theorems. For the two-row periodic Ising torus we give the exact reflection factorization of the row transfer matrix, reduce the crossing at zeta = i to a real cubic, and identify the critical coupling a_c* = 0.8637850566870... as the unique root in (0,1) of an explicit octic. We prove that every a > a_c* satisfies the arc condition simultaneously for all circumferences, that no smaller coupling does, and that the finite thresholds approach a_c* at the rate C/n^2 with an explicit algebraic constant C. The factorization and the 2x2 threshold are formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib; the zeta = i reduction, uniformity and rate are analysis-level.

title: On nearly Lefschetz fibrations and spinal open books
abstract: We survey the recent development of spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations. The focus is on explaining past and new results regarding the detection of symplectic fillability and classification of symplectic fillings of contact 3-manifolds in light of the new machinery. We give many examples and a list of open questions. This can be considered as an additional chapter to the lecture notes by Ozbacgi and Wendl.

title: Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
abstract: We construct binary codes that attain the classical Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy guarantee for a fixed number of edit errors, with deterministic polynomial-time construction, encoding, and decoding. For every fixed integer $t\ge 1$ and all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, our codes correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions in total, with redundancy at most $2t\log_2 n+O_t(1)$. All algorithms run in polynomial time in $n$ for fixed $t$, and decoding recovers the original information message. This realizes the classical counting guarantee algorithmically without enumerating the exponentially large space of binary words.

title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $ρ$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some instances of modularity in this situation. Our main result is that $ρ$ is modular if it is non-split at every place above $p$ where it is reducible, by combining Zhang's pro-modularity theorem with a classicality criterion based on Emerton's ordinary parts. Together with a theorem of Zhao on local indecomposability, this gives the modularity of the $λ$-adic representations attached to abelian varieties of $\GL_2$-type in the mixed case, and, using a result of Snowden, of potentially modular representations of parallel weight two under a mild additional condition. It also gives the modularity of representations whose local type at every place above $p$ is of discrete series type, and, through a member of the compatible system with interchanged Hodge-Tate weights, of potentially modular representations of weight $(2,k)$ over real quadratic fields with Steinberg type at one place above $p$, under conditions on that member.

title: The first non-trivial Fučík curve for the sublinear Dirichlet Laplacian
abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open connected set, and let $q\in(1,2)$. We consider the sublinear $q$-eigenvalue problem for the Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δu=λ\|u\|_{L^q(Ω)}^{2-q}|u|^{q-2}u$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)\setminus\{0\}$, whose first eigenvalue $λ_1(Ω)$ is simple, with eigenfunctions of constant sign. The definition of a second eigenvalue is not unique. Following the approach introduced by Molle and Passaseo for the linear Laplacian, we construct the first non-trivial curve of the corresponding Fučík spectrum, and show that it has a unique diagonal point $(γ(Ω),γ(Ω))$. The Fučík-selected second value $λ_2^F(Ω)=2^{1-\frac{2}{q}}γ(Ω)$ is strictly larger than $λ_1(Ω)$, admits a two-phase variational characterisation, and satisfies a sharp Hong-Krahn-Szegő inequality: among sets of given measure it is minimised by the union of two equal balls. The selected solution at the diagonal point is a classical $(2,q)$-eigenfunction exactly when its nodal $L^q$-masses are balanced. We finally show that on balls in dimensions $N\geq2$ every Fučík-selected solution is foliated Schwarz symmetric.

title: Well-Covered Powers: Cartesian Products and Cayley Graphs
abstract: We study graphs whose powers are well-covered, with an emphasis on Cartesian products and Cayley graphs. We first establish necessary conditions and sufficient criteria for Cartesian products, provide examples showing that a factor need not be well-covered and that two noncomplete factors can have the well-covered powers property, and classify several structured product families. In particular, we construct graphs satisfying the well-covered powers property for arbitrarily large diameters. We then show that the Cartesian square of a connected abelian Cayley graph is well-covered exactly when the graph is complete. We classify the well-covered-power graphs among connected circulant graphs of degree at most four. For Cartesian products of any number of complete graphs, we also prove that the recursive alphabet-size inequalities in the final conjecture are sufficient for all powers to be well-covered, prove partial converses for arbitrarily many factors, and give explicit obstructions for every binary prefix followed by one complete factor.

title: Exact penalty methods with adaptive discretization for nonsmooth semi-infinite optimization
abstract: The paper considers a nonsmooth semi-infinite optimization problem in which the constraints are reformulated through a value function. Stationary points of the cutting surface approximations are studied, showing that stationarity is preserved in the limit under boundedness of the associated sequence of multipliers. Building on these results, an algorithm that combines the cutting surface approximations with a penalty scheme is devised, together with some proximal variants. An exact penalty result is established under suitable global conditions, and numerical results are reported to compare the methods with existing exact penalty and cutting surface algorithms.

title: A probabilistic score estimation using the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula
abstract: Score-learning methods generally lack pointwise supervision, which affects the training accuracy, particularly in regions where SDE trajectories are rare. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel method called \emph{BEL anchors}, which uses Monte Carlo score estimates at user-selected space-time query points. By combining a Feynman--Kac representation of the Fokker--Planck equation with the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula, our estimator requires neither closed-form transition densities, spatial discretization, nor derivatives of the initial density. We derive its asymptotic variance and use the anchors as sparse supervised targets for existing score-learning objectives. Experiments show that BEL anchors improve implicit score matching in poorly sampled regions, prevent score-PINN collapse, and enable accurate sample regeneration in several numerical examples.

title: On silting theory for complete path algebras
abstract: Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $Λ$ be the complete path algebra of $Q$ with respect to the arrow ideal. We study the mutation of silting objects in the bounded homotopy category of projective $Λ$-modules and characterise in which cases the mutation theories of silting complexes and 2-term silting complexes of $Λ$ are determined by those of a finite dimensional quotient $Λ/I$. This characterisation is closely related to a characterisation of 2-term silting finite quotient algebras.

title: Weighted Randomized Kaczmarz for Sparsely Corrupted Linear Systems
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalized weighted randomized Kaczmarz framework to approximate solutions to overdetermined linear systems whose measurements are perturbed by sparse, additive corruptions. The proposed framework samples equations with probabilities proportional to a user-defined weighting function of their corresponding residual magnitudes. Our work focuses on weighting functions that will reduce the influence of potentially corrupted equations, and provides analyses for a general class of non-increasing weighting functions. We derive one-step expected squared error bounds that separate progress on uncorrupted equations from the contribution of corrupted equations, and provide sufficient conditions for geometric convergence under one specific family of weighting functions -- threshold weighting. We also investigate adaptive exponential weights scaled by the median or median absolute deviation of residual magnitudes, requiring no prior knowledge of the corruption fraction or magnitudes. Lastly, we consider a family of inverse residual weighting functions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefit of such a generalized framework in its flexibility in developing approaches for settings in which information about the corruptions is known or unknown.

title: Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs
abstract:
We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions.
  For polyhedral products, we combine these results with their description by relative graph products and graph products of pairs. We also obtain bounds and exact computations for amenable category, together with applications to simplicial volume and Borel rigidity of closed aspherical polyhedral-product manifolds.

title: D-equivalence conjecture for hyperkähler varieties of generalized Kummer type
abstract: We show that birationally equivalent hyperkähler varieties of generalized Kummer type are derived equivalent, confirming the D-equivalence conjecture in this case. Combined with recent results of other authors, this settles the conjecture for all known deformation types of hyperkähler varieties. The kernel is built from an equivariant Fourier-Mukai kernel on the sum-zero loci of powers of an abelian surface. We deform it along diagonal twistor paths, using the hyperholomorphic endomorphism algebra. Comparing wall hyperplanes gives a common twisted derived category for two adjacent birational models, and a finite sequence of wall crossings then gives the equivalence.

title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
abstract:
We study fractional coloring with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle in which one seeks a probability distribution on the independent sets of a graph such that each vertex $v$ is included with probability at least a prescribed target $φ(v)$. For $K_r$-free graphs, Kelly and Postle conjectured that such a distribution exists provided $φ(v)\le c_r\frac{\log d(v)}{d(v)}$ for a fixed \(c_r>0\), where $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$, and they established this up to a factor of $(\log\log d(v))^2$. In this paper, we prove their conjecture, showing that \[
  φ(v)\le\frac{c}{r}\frac{\log(d(v)+2)}{d(v)+1} \] suffices for an absolute constant $c>0$. As a corollary, we obtain a lower bound on the independence number of $K_r$-free graphs in terms of their degree sequence. This strengthens the bound that OpenAI proved in resolving the Ajtai-Erdős-Komlós-Szemerédi conjecture. Moreover, our argument yields a deterministic algorithm that produces the desired probability distribution in time $2^{O(r^2)}n^{O(1)}$, where \(n\) is the number of vertices and the implied constants are absolute.

title: Optimal Communication for Distributed Sparse Histogram Aggregation
abstract:
Histogram estimation is a fundamental primitive in distributed data analysis, with applications in counting queries and federated learning. In many settings, the universe of categories is enormous, yet each user's data involves only a small subset, yielding sparse local histograms. This raises a natural question: To what extent can local sparsity reduce the communication needed to estimate the global histogram?
  We answer this question by characterizing the communication complexity of distributed sparse histogram estimation under prescribed $\ell_1$ distortion and failure probability constraints. Our upper bound is achieved by a randomized covering scheme that optimizes how accurately each user represents its local histogram to reduce communication. By exploiting the distortion budget directly rather than imposing unbiasedness, the scheme achieves lower communication costs than standard unbiased sampling and hashing constructions. We establish the scheme's first-order optimality through a lower bound based on local support identification. The key step is to relate communication cost directly to the number of active coordinates revealed by each user's message, rather than to bound information about the aggregate via distance-based Fano's inequalities. This characterization further quantifies how the communication advantage of heterogeneous over homogeneous encoders varies across parameter regimes.

title: It is time for a New Deal for mathematics
abstract: The AI labs' vision is based on extraction (of data, wealth, and political power). Mathematicians must oppose it, moving past personal reflections and towards reforming mathematics' social contract.

title: Long-time behaviour and bifurcation analysis of a non-reciprocal two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the torus
abstract: A two-species aggregation-diffusion system on the one-dimensional torus with antisymmetric cross-interactions modeling pursuit-evasion dynamics is studied. The self-interaction strength is used as a bifurcation parameter, and the linear stability of the homogeneous state is characterized by Fourier analysis. It is shown that non-reciprocal coupling enlarges the stability region. In a symmetric diffusion setting, exponential convergence to the homogeneous state is established for sufficiently weak self-interactions by means of an entropy argument, with a decay condition independent of the cross-interaction strength. Under suitable nondegeneracy and spectral assumptions, the first loss of stability is shown to occur through a Hopf bifurcation associated with a single spatial Fourier mode. A branch of time-periodic patterns is thereby obtained, along which the two species oscillate with a fixed phase difference. An explicit formula for the cubic Hopf coefficient is derived, and an essential dependence of the direction and stability of the bifurcating branch on the second spatial harmonic is identified. In the case of matching diffusion coefficients and interaction kernels, sufficiently strong non-reciprocity is shown to transform a subcritical stationary instability of the corresponding reciprocal system into a supercritical Hopf bifurcation with stable periodic solutions. An exchange-of-stability result is proved, and the theory is illustrated for Kuramoto, two-mode cosine, and top-hat interaction kernels.

title: Every classifiable simple C*-algebra has a C*-diagonal
abstract: We construct C*-diagonals in all UCT Kirchberg algebras. Together with known constructions of C*-diagonals in the stably finite setting by Xin Li, this shows that every classifiable C*-algebra (in the sense of the Elliott classification programme) has a C*-diagonal. In fact, we show that every UCT Kirchberg algebra admits an untwisted principal étale groupoid model with a finite-dimensional unit space.

title: K3 Categories and Mukai Homomorphisms for Debarre-Voisin Varieties
abstract: Let $M=X_6^σ$ be a smooth Debarre-Voisin hyperkähler fourfold and $X=X_3^σ$ the associated smooth hyperplane section of $\operatorname{Gr}(3,10)$. Using the incidence correspondence between $X$ and $M$, we construct a family $\mathcal E$ of objects in the Kuznetsov component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$. We write $v$ for the common Mukai vector of its fibers. We prove that the associated Mukai homomorphism \[ Θ_{\mathcal E}|_{v^\perp}\colon v^\perp\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(M,\mathbb Z) \] is an integral Hodge isometry and explicitly determine the inverse image of the Plücker polarization. For a very general point of the trivector divisor corresponding to discriminant $24$, we also construct an integral Hodge isometry between the full Mukai lattices of $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$ and the associated twisted K3 surface.

title: Estimating "Realized" Skewness using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: We propose a new estimator of low-frequency skewness (monthly) that exploits high-frequency data (5 min) through a direct functional mapping consisting of layers of Convolutional Neural Networks followed by Multi Layer Perceptrons. Monte Carlo experiments involving stochastic volatility models, with and without jumps, show that the estimator reduces finite-sample bias relative to existing realized-skewness estimators and remains accurate under model misspecification. Empirically, our estimator exhibits temporal stability and delivers cross-sectional performance in actual skewness-sorted portfolios. We characterize the finite-sample bias of conventional plug-in skewness estimators and establish risk consistency properties of the proposed NN estimator under standard regularity conditions.

title: Fat base schemes and unexpected hypersurfaces of type $(d+k,d)$
abstract:
We study hypersurfaces of degree $d+k$ containing a prescribed zero-dimensional fat point scheme $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ and having multiplicity at least $d$ along a general codimension-two linear subspace. We associate with this interpolation problem a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ whose splitting type determines the dimensions of all linear systems of type $(d+k,d)$.
  For a fat point of multiplicity $m$, we determine the exact number of conditions detected by this bundle and introduce the corresponding effective length. This leads to an excess formula separating the contributions of the splitting type, the part of the fat structure invisible to degree-$k$ fibrewise sections, and the Hilbert-function defect of the fixed scheme.
  We also prove a truncation theorem showing that multiplicities larger than $k$ contribute only a uniform twist of the bundle and, geometrically, fixed hyperplane components. Finally, we exhibit explicit planar and three-dimensional examples showing that genuinely unexpected phenomena persist for nonreduced fixed base schemes, including geometrically irreducible unexpected hypersurfaces.

title: Exotic Dehn twists on sums of 4-manifolds, nuclei, and exotic structures
abstract: For closed 4-manifolds $X_1, X_2$, we give a sufficient condition, in terms of the Seiberg-Witten invariants of $X_i$, for the Dehn twist on $X_1\#X_2$ along the neck to be smoothly nontrivial. This provides a broad generalization of the result of Kronheimer-Mrowka for $K3\#K3$. We also show that the boundary Dehn twists on the punctured connected sums of many pairs of elliptic surfaces are smoothly nontrivial. We also detect new examples of exotic Dehn twists along Seifert fibered 3-manifolds in elliptic surfaces. As a consequence, we exhibit a new phenomenon in which "exotic diffeomorphisms detect exotic smooth structures on 4-manifolds": the triviality of the boundary Dehn twist characterizes the standard nucleus $N(n)$ among the nuclei $N(n)_{p,q}$ homeomorphic to it, provided that $n\equiv0 \bmod 4$. These results are proved by computing the families Bauer-Furuta invariant for a new framing of the families Dirac index.

title: Unstable Stokes waves in constant vorticity flows of infinite depth
abstract: We study the spectral stability of small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in infinite depth. We describe the spectrum near the origin and near the first nonzero double eigenvalue. For nonzero vorticity $ω<2\sqrt{g/3}$, where $g$ is the gravitational constant, the eigenvalues near the origin form a figure eight, whereas for $ω>2\sqrt{g/3}$ the local spectrum remains purely imaginary. Away from the origin, the interaction of two Fourier modes whose indices differ by two produces an unstable isola when $ω>-\sqrt{g/6}$, $ω\ne0$, and the resonant wave numbers are noninteger. This curve is a real analytic oval with an explicit leading ellipse and maximal growth of quadratic order in the amplitude. We also prove instability at the integer resonances needed to cover the remaining vorticities. Together with the classical irrotational result, these two mechanisms show that sufficiently small nonzero Stokes waves are spectrally unstable for every fixed constant vorticity. The proof uses finite-dimensional spectral reductions of the full Euler linearization. Near the origin, the finite-dimensional linearized operator has a one-sided limit as the Floquet exponent vanishes, which differs from the periodic linearization. We use the Kato transformation to construct a three-dimensional reduction with biorthogonal bases and use all three eigenvectors of the reference operator to calculate the Benjamin--Feir coefficient. At the nonzero collision, a real two-dimensional reduction and an explicit second-order calculation determine the unstable curve.

title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

title: Unstable Stokes waves in constant vorticity flows of finite depth
abstract: We study the spectral instability of small-amplitude Stokes waves in finite-depth flows with constant vorticity. A center-manifold reduction and the periodic Evans function give two explicit indices, one for long-wave instability near the origin and the other for an order-two resonance away from the origin. We prove instability when the low-frequency index is positive or the high-frequency index is nonzero, and obtain the leading expansions of the unstable spectral points. At low frequency, first- and second-order monodromy coefficients determine the leading figure-eight curve. At high frequency, we prove that the resonance exists uniquely and derive a limiting ellipse. An algebraic identity expresses the high-frequency index as a positive factor times the square of a real coupling coefficient. Thus every parameter pair with nonzero coupling gives high-frequency instability. The explicit formulas also permit a comparison of the two criteria in the parameter plane.

title: Nuisance structure and the detection boundary for population size: how profiling can change a rate, not only a constant
abstract: A system contains an unknown number $N$ of units, each failing at an unknown common rate, each unit is removed once it fails. The failure-rate declines as units are removed, but after only a few failures the decline is too slight to distinguish from a constant rate, and the maximum-likelihood estimate of $N$ is infinite with substantial probability. This is a well-known feature of the model, but its probability has not been quantified. We show that about $N^{2/3}$ failures are needed before a finite population can be distinguished from an inexhaustible one, and that at this scale the profile log-likelihood ratio converges to that of a Gaussian shift experiment, in which an infinite estimate occurs with a calculable probability. The exponent is not a property of the model alone. Profiling annihilates the Taylor terms that the nuisance-parameters can reproduce, and detectability is governed by the first surviving term. For example, unknown drift in testing-effort reproduces the linear term, leaving a quadratic survivor and raising the requirement to $N^{4/5}$; in general the critical scale is $N^{2q/(2q+1)}$ for a survivor of order $q$. We obtain the limiting-law of the estimator, the null likelihood ratio distribution, and confidence sets that may be unbounded.

title: Mixed-Integer Program Sensitivity Analysis via Branch-and-Bound Trees
abstract: We study how to compute valid dual bounds for mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) with finite variable bounds under data perturbations. In an offline-online setting, a nominal instance is solved once and its information is reused to evaluate perturbations. We develop a framework for linear programs under simultaneous perturbations to the objective coefficients, right-hand side, and constraint matrix. Our construction is based on a bounded Lagrangian dual evaluated at nominal optimal dual multipliers. We prove that its gap to the perturbed LP optimal value grows at most linearly with perturbation magnitude under suitable conditions. We extend this construction to MILPs by reusing the nominal branch-and-bound tree and node-level dual information, generalizing the sensitivity analysis framework of Schrage and Wolsey (1985) to all problem data. To strengthen the dual bounds, we adapt their subtree-selection dynamic program. The online computations support GPU acceleration and highly parallel evaluation of dual bounds, which can also certify optimal variable fixings and accelerate reoptimization. Experiments on generalized independent set, combinatorial auction, capacitated facility location, and unit commitment instances produce tight dual bounds at low computational cost. For single-parameter ``what-if'' perturbations, gaps are typically a small fraction of a percent, with GPU evaluation times below a millisecond per perturbation. Relative to the time Gurobi needs to obtain bounds of the same quality, GPU evaluation is approximately 2,000--240,000 times faster for single-parameter perturbations and 120--50,000 times faster for multi-parameter perturbations. Using exact perturbed optima as supplied primal cutoffs, variable fixing accelerates exact reoptimization by up to a factor of 10 for generalized independent set instances, with little or no improvement for unit commitment.

title: Pairwise Distortion Distribution with Graph-Based Importance Sampling for Quantization Error and Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
abstract: Quantifying the dimensionality of data is a fundamental need in machine learning and signal processing applications such as representation learning, data compression, and inverse problems, where the extrinsic dimension in which the data is presented can be very different from the intrinsic dimension that determines the operational performance. Various concepts, such as Rényi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension are useful here. Despite their theoretical significance, estimating these measures are challenging given their asymptotic definitions. Recent research has shown that analyzing the pairwise distortion distribution (PDD) of a data source can provide a tractable lower bound on the distortion of random codebook quantization, from which a tractable notion of intrinsic dimension can be derived. In this paper we extend this line of research in three main ways. First, we develop a related upper bound on distortion of random codebook quantization. Second, we improve the computability of both the lower and upper bounds, using a graph-based adaptive importance sampling approach. Third, we leverage the bounds to define new notions of intrinsic dimension which form upper and lower bounds on the Rényi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension, and which can be empirically estimated from unknown data sources. We illustrate the concepts by analyzing several artificial and empirical distributions.

title: Scaling laws for linear-elastic two-variant martensitic phase transitions in general domains
abstract: We consider a two-well problem within geometrically linear elasticity, on a bounded Lipschitz set in dimension $n\ge 2$. We assume that the two wells are compatible through a symmetrized rank-one connection and that the displacement matches their average on the boundary, and we include a regularization based on the total surface energy. We show that there are two distinct regimes, with the energy scaling differently in terms of the surface-energy coefficient $\eps$: it is proportional to $\eps^{2/3}$ if there are two distinct compatible twin-normal directions, and to $\eps^{4/5}$ if there is only one. This matches previous findings in rectangles and other special geometries, mostly in two dimensions, and the lower bounds obtained by a Fourier method by Raiţă, Rüland, Tissot and Tribuzio (2024). Our results are obtained by explicit constructions, which contain a self-similar refinement of oscillations close to the boundary, and by a short real-space proof of the matching lower bounds.

title: Relative-Error Composite Federated Optimization with One Server-Side Proximal Step per Round
abstract: We consider deterministic composite federated optimization, in which distributed smooth client objectives are combined with a shared, possibly nonsmooth, regularizer. We propose Relative-Error Composite FedDyn (REC-FedDyn), an inexact method that supports partial participation, with one server-side proximal evaluation per communication round. REC-FedDyn employs a directly testable relative-error criterion that allows each client to independently control the accuracy of its local subproblem, without a server-side acceptance test. We establish almost-sure iterate convergence for strongly convex and convex problems, almost-sure asymptotic stationarity for nonconvex problems, and communication and parallel gradient-evaluation complexity bounds, all under partial participation and without assuming bounded data heterogeneity. Experiments on image inpainting, fMRI prediction, and neural-network classification with structured regularization demonstrate efficiency and robustness across levels of data heterogeneity and client participation.

title: Co-Decompositions and FO Model Checking
abstract:
Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition.
  Our main contribution is an algorithmic meta-theorem for first order logic: given only a co-decomposition of a $σ$-structure $G$ with $b$ bags, each of size at most $w$ and an FO sentence $φ$, there is an algorithm which, without ever constructing or inspecting $G$, operates on the co-decomposition and determines whether $G \models φ$ in time $f_σ(w,|\varphi|)\cdot b$. We pair this algorithm with structural results on tree co-width, including its relationship to tree-width and a separation from twin-width. Furthermore, we characterize bounded path co-width using a graph grammar. In contrast to our logical meta-theorem, we prove that $(s,t)$-Path becomes NP-hard on co-decomposition inputs. These results demonstrate how categorical constructions can enable efficient computation on exponentially compressed structures.

title: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series
abstract: The achievable precision in estimating the spectrum of a time-series signal that is promised to be sparse in Fourier space deteriorates rapidly as the spectral peaks get closer together, as soon as we introduce noise. Here, we study the related task of generator estimation: estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time-series and its eigenvalues. We obtain rigorous non-asymptotic precision guarantees on genESPRIT, a practical algorithm solving generator estimation, and show that this task can be solved with precision independent of the spectral spacing. The guarantees are complemented by a Cramér--Rao analysis of a relaxation of the problem. In particular, in the case of unitary data with bounded additive noise with effective entrywise variance $σ^2$, we show that genESPRIT estimates the associated propagator matrix in Frobenius norm with precision scaling as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(σNL^{-\frac12})$ in the length of the time-series $L$ and matrix dimension $N$, matching the corresponding spectrum-independent Cramér--Rao standard deviation scaling up to logarithmic factors. We prove that the matching distance error in the spectrum estimated by genESPRIT scales as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (σ^2 N^3 L^{-1} + σN^{\frac32} L^{-\frac32} )$, which we compare to the lower bound on the corresponding Cramér--Rao bound with the asymptotic standard deviation scaling $\mathcal{O}(σL^{-\frac32})$. These guarantees provide the first rigorous bounds on solving the generator estimation problem. As the matrix exponential time-series can be obtained from linearly independent vector time-series by concatenation, this work opens up a new direction in spectral estimation, which circumvents the problem of crowded spectra, under the additional assumption of linear independence.

title: Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups
abstract: Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. We also prove that the (outer) automorphism group of any free-by-cyclic group $M=F\rtimes_\varphi\mathbb{Z}$ is of type $\rm{VF}$, and so are the McCool subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(M)$. This relies on the construction of a new $\mathrm{Out}(M)$-invariant splitting of $M$, that enables us to reduce the proof of the above statements to the case where the outer class of $\varphi$ has finite order.

title: Lorentz-Invariant Measure for Path Integrals in the Future Cone
abstract:
We construct a measure on continuous paths in the future cone of two-dimensional space that is invariant under the orthochronous Lorentz group and quasi-invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group.
  We use the proposed measure to obtain the fundamental solution of the heat equation. The result agrees with the expression obtained by other methods.

title: Local convexity obstructions for bounded realizations of Teichmüller space
abstract: Let $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded domain that is biholomorphic to a finite-dimensional Teichmüller space. We prove that $\partial D$ has no locally convex boundary patch containing a complex $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold through each of its points. Note that in complex dimension two this excludes every locally convex boundary point, without any boundary regularity assumption. In every dimension, we also exclude locally convex $C^2$ boundary patches.

title: Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions
abstract: We give a proof that an isolated algebraic symplectic singularity of dimension $2n\ge 4$ admitting a projective symplectic resolution is analytically isomorphic to the minimal nilpotent orbit closure in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ at the origin.

title: Continuized Quasar-Convex Acceleration via an Unbiased Finite-Mixing Network Oracle
abstract: We study decentralized minimization of a smooth network average that is globally quasar-convex with respect to a fixed minimizer; the node functions may be nonconvex and need not share a minimizer. A unit-rate Poisson clock drives an exactly simulable continuized process: between events the state follows a closed-form accelerated flow, and each event uses one oracle vector. One master theorem covers oracles with a predictable bias and a state-dependent variance and keeps the inverse-quadratic term $\mathcal{O}(LR_0^2/(γ^2T^2))$; one selected-row lemma supplies the oracle moments of three network implementations. CQA-Net keeps a common state, mixes local rows for finitely many rounds, and disseminates one uniformly selected row; its oracle is unbiased at every mixing depth, so incomplete averaging affects only the variance. A walking token removes dissemination, the shared clock, and the shared root, and an importance weight keeps it unbiased on fixed graphs. D-CQA keeps local states and mixes them; under bounded heterogeneity it needs $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrtχ\sqrt{L}R_0/(γθ\sqrt{\varepsilon}))$ communication rounds and no dissemination. Changing graphs enter through certified operator norms. Experiments on a certified nonconvex regression on static and changing graphs compare the three implementations.

title: System-level performance in massive ISAC networks
abstract: We propose a dynamic stochastic geometry framework to model and evaluate large-scale integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. Base stations are distributed according to a homogeneous Poisson point process, while user equipments and sensing objects undergo localised random motion around their serving base station. Full spectrum reuse with a common waveform generates mutual interference that couples the two functionalities. Communication performance is characterised through downlink queues whose service rates are governed by the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) via the Shannon capacity. Sensing performance is captured by a Kalman filter (KF) whose measurement noise covariance depends on the sensing SINR, yielding a non-classical state-dependent filtering problem. We define system-level performance metrics under the Palm distribution of the base station process and prove the consistency of their empirical estimators. We then prove that, for a typical base station, communication and sensing metrics are associated, so that operating regimes favourable to one functionality tend to benefit the other. The proof combines the monotonicity of the queue and filter recursions in the configuration of interferers with the Harris--FKG inequality for Poisson functionals. We also show that the excess association ratio of the two interference levels decays as the inverse of the network density. Simulations based on a ray-tracing channel model corroborate the analysis.

title: Nonlinear Darcy Laws for Generalized Newtonian Fluids with Orlicz Growth and Oscillating Navier Slip in Periodic Porous Media
abstract: We study the periodic homogenization of a stationary generalized Navier--Stokes system in a periodically perforated domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\in\{2,3\}$, with a heterogeneous bulk stress of general Orlicz growth and an oscillating nonlinear Navier friction law on the pore walls, both at the Darcy scale. If the lower growth exponent at infinity satisfies $p^-_\infty>3N/(N+2)$ and the inertial exponent exceeds $κ_c:=1+N(2/p^-_\infty-1)_+$, inertia vanishes and, under strict monotonicity of the bulk stress, the whole family converges to the nonlinear Darcy law $U=\mathcal K(f-\nabla p_0)$, $\operatorname{div}U=0$, $U\cdotν=0$. The permeability map $\mathcal K$ is continuous, strictly monotone, obeys two-sided Orlicz bounds and incorporates the wall slip through a nonlinear cell problem, and the extended microscopic pressure converges strongly to $p_0$. The proof relies on a uniform Orlicz--Korn inequality, a Darcy-scaled two-scale trace theorem and a coupled bulk--surface Minty argument.

title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
abstract: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(κ>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-κ}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.

title: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding and Antenna Positioning for Movable-Antenna MU-MIMO Systems
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) improve wireless communications by adapting antenna positions to the propagation environment. However, antenna movement also changes the mutual coupling (MC) among elements of the transmit and receive arrays, which affects the performance of MA-enabled systems. In this paper, we investigate MC-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system with MAs at both the base station and users. We establish an MC-aware system model by combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based representation of the transmit and receive arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem that jointly optimizes multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The problem is challenging because the precoders and positions are coupled through the propagation channels and position-dependent MC matrices. To address this challenge, we reformulate the problem in the antenna-current domain to to efficiently handle the MC matrices and develop a current-domain weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework for alternating optimization. Furthermore, we handle the nonconvex position updates within the framework by using majorization--minimization (MM) and solve the resulting convex subproblems with a dedicated conic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design improves the WSR over both an MC-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores MC during optimization.

title: Eigenstates on $O^\ast$-algebras with an application to ladder operators
abstract: Following some recent results, we consider here a particular class of states on a $O^\ast$-algebra $\M$ which we call {\em eigenstates of an element} $A\in\M$, and we deduce some of their properties. Then, we apply our definition to a family of ladder elements, i.e. elements of $\M$ obeying certain algebraic (commutation) relations which are physically motivated, and we discuss several results for these states

title: Local resolution of the second log-Fitting ideal
abstract: Logarithmic Fitting ideals encode the complexity of the corresponding morphisms in a natural and intrinsic way, and their principalisation offers a new perspective on problems such as the resolution of cotangent sheaves and the monomialisation of morphisms. In this paper, we give a local resolution theorem for log-rank adapted morphisms: after finite sequences of smooth local blow-ups, the first two log-Fitting ideals \mathcal{F}\_{n--1}(σ) and \mathcal{F}\_{n--2}(σ) become principal monomial ideals.

title: Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff for Vector Gaussian Sources with Limited Common Randomness: Exact Characterization and Approximate Universality
abstract: The distortion-rate-common randomness-perception (DRCP) theory characterizes how limited common randomness (CR) improves reconstruction fidelity under perceptual constraints, thereby providing an information-theoretic foundation for generative compression. In this paper, we characterize the DRCP tradeoff for vector Gaussian sources with limited CR under the squared-error distortion measure and the squared Wasserstein-2 perception measure. Specifically, we first establish a generalized reverse waterfilling characterization of globally optimal allocations. Second, we derive an analytical upper bound on the DRCP function through sequential greedy allocation of rate and CR. For fixed rate and CR budgets, the resulting representation is independent of the perception threshold. Finally, we establish its approximate universality through uniform performance guarantees: the achievable distortion exceeds the optimal distortion by at most $2ρ^*\approx0.2897$ times the total source variance, whereas the optimal-to-greedy distortion ratio is at least $η^*\approx0.7517$.

title: A Relative Telescope-Type Conjecture: Support and Generation in Half-Bounded Derived Categories
abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative noetherian ring. We ask whether complexes with finitely generated cohomology and a fixed support can be generated by relatively compact objects, using coproducts which exist in the half-bounded derived category. We prove that $\mathbf D^+_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathrm{ex}}(\mathbf D^b_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R))$ whenever $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec} R$ is specialization closed and has finite dimension. The same equality holds for every specialization-closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ when $B$ is a finite-type algebra over a noetherian domain $A$ of finite character and either $A$ or $B$ is regular. These equalities classify the thick Hom-submodules closed under existing coproducts. We also prove the corresponding bounded-above statement from the support results of Matsui--Takahashi. For an arbitrary noetherian ring, the bounded-below generation conjecture reduces to torsion complexes over quotient domains, with their support unchanged. Finally, over a regular noetherian domain of infinite dimension, we give a bounded-below object which is generated by bounded objects with the same support but has no bounded-below representative by finitely generated modules. The comparison functor from the bounded-below derived category of finite modules is therefore neither full nor essentially surjective.

title: A sharp Mittag-Leffler bound for series with separated exponents
abstract: Let $η\geq 0$ and $δ>0$, and let $(r_j)_{j\geq 0}$ be a sequence of real numbers satisfying $η\leq r_0 < r_1 < r_2 < \cdots$ and $r_{j+1}-r_j \geq δ$ for every $j\geq 0$. We prove that, for $δ\leq 1$ and every $x>0$, \[ \sum_{j=0}^\infty \frac{x^{r_j}}{\G(1+r_j)} \leq \sum_{j=0}^\infty \frac{x^{η+jδ}}{\G(1+η+jδ)} = x^ηE_{δ,1+η}(x^δ), \] where $E_{δ,1+η}$ denotes the two-parameter Mittag-Leffler function. Moreover, equality holds for some $x>0$ if and only if $r_j = η+ jδ$ for every $j$. The proof combines a finite compression argument for unimodal functions with a shift inequality for the Mittag-Leffler function. The upper bound $δ\leq 1$ is sharp, since counterexamples exist for every $1 < δ< 2$.

title: Star-shaped periodic solutions of a system of delay differential equations: A computer-assisted proof
abstract: In this paper, we consider a planar system of nonlinear delay differential equations and prove the existence of the star-shaped periodic solutions conjectured by Hara (Nonlinear Analysis: Theory, Methods \& Applications, 30:4555--4563 (1997)) for seven parameter values. These solutions cannot be obtained by a direct application of the standard Fourier spectral method, since the corresponding linearized operator is degenerate. From numerical observations of the Fourier coefficients, we derive an ansatz that writes a star-shaped periodic solution as a periodic profile in a rotating frame. Restricting the profile to real Fourier coefficients, we show that the resonance between the delay and the period of the profile fixes the rotation frequency exactly. We then validate a zero of the resulting real system with the radii polynomial approach and interval arithmetic, with bounds that cover all Fourier modes. For each parameter value, we also determine the fundamental period and the winding number of the solution.

title: A hybrid quantum-classical lattice kinetic scheme with tensor-train feedback for incompressible flows
abstract: Nonlinear lattice kinetic simulation requires each updated distribution to supply the velocity and gradients that determine the next step. In a quantum-classical solver, reading out the full distribution incurs work proportional to the lattice size. We construct a tensor-train (TT) interface that retains reusable classical cores at the physical amplitude scale for a full-relaxation lattice kinetic scheme. The cores supply nonlinear coefficients and prepare each quantum input. Energy-scaled propagation and coordinate recovery encode the updated distribution, and alternating least-squares reconstruction converts signed Hadamard-test overlaps into output cores by restoring a known normalization factor. The next step starts from accepted cores without replaying previous quantum evolution. Under positive, unit-sum reference coefficients, positive lower and finite upper density bounds, and Lipschitz equilibrium sensitivity, perturbation bounds relate local defects to feedback errors. Resource bounds account for classical operations, circuit execution, sampling, and verification. Classical diagnostics expose why distribution accuracy alone is insufficient: in 80-step feedback on a $16\times16$ grid, rank cap 4 nearly eliminates the vortex despite a final distribution error below $1\%$, whereas rank cap 12 gives relative velocity error $1.03\times10^{-3}$. Four-step binomial readout simulations show that tightening core sampling tolerance threefold raises the prescribed sufficient budget from $5.97\times10^{12}$ to $5.37\times10^{13}$ shots as the result approaches the fixed-rank, fixed-sweep exact-overlap trajectory. The interface therefore provides a way to connect quantum propagation to nonlinear feedback and to assess the separate demands of compression, velocity accuracy, and readout precision.

title: Singular solutions from simple Euclidean Jordan algebras
abstract: For every finite-dimensional simple Euclidean Jordan algebra $V$ of rank at least three, we realize the function $\operatorname{tr}(x^3)/|x|$ on its traceless subspace $V_0$ as a $C^{1,1}\setminus C^2$ viscosity solution of a uniformly elliptic equation $F(D^2 u)=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^{\operatorname{dim}V_0}$. This unifies and extends earlier constructions from Cartan isoparametric cubics, Hsiang minimal cubics, and traceless real symmetric matrices.

title: RH-Conditional Positivity in a Theta-Kernel Langevin Model
abstract: A classical Brownian-bridge representation of Riemann's xi function defines an even, rapidly confining probability density and a reversible Langevin model. Our principal physical observable is the transient variance after a quadratic-potential quench; we also analyze a tilted bridge-range response and a sixth-order cumulant gap. For a specified passive harmonic trap with bounded delayed residual feedback, we derive a non-vacuous finite-time variance-increase bound under explicit calibration and sampling assumptions. An elementary global curvature estimate and de Bruijn's strip-contraction theorem give a direct proof of a strict susceptibility bound for every nonnegative quadratic tilt, without assuming the Riemann hypothesis. The inequality itself is a classical GHS consequence, valid more generally for every real quadratic tilt. Reversibility then gives explicit finite-time response and deterministic-control action bounds (not thermodynamic energy). The same curvature estimate gives monotone variance relaxation after an outward quadratic quench, with an exponential deficit bound. At the undeformed density, all alternating zero-field cumulant signs and the displayed low-order cumulant gap are also unconditional; neither is an RH test. The genuinely stronger RH-conditional structure is a positive Stieltjes representation and positive semidefiniteness of divided-difference matrices of every size. At the undeformed density that entire matrix hierarchy is equivalent to RH. We separate these exact statements from finite-sample confidence bounds, numerical discretization evidence, and theoretical physical implementations. The work supplies neither a proof of RH nor a laboratory realization.

title: Ramified tori and Gelfand--Kirillov dimension of mod $p$ representations
abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension of degree $n$ with $p\geq3$, and let $D$ be the non-split quaternion algebra over $K$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional admissible smooth representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(K)$ or $D^\times$ with a central character and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition has Gelfand--Kirillov dimension $n$. As a corollary, every infinite-dimensional admissible Banach representation whose locally analytic vectors have an infinitesimal character has dimension $n$, strengthening Sorgdrager's bound to an equality. An appendix by Yongquan Hu proves that, when $K\ne\mathbb{Q}_p$ and the coefficient field is algebraically closed, the canonical diagram of an admissible supersingular representation satisfying the same Casimir annihilation condition is $(π,π,\mathrm{id})$, as in the case of local fields of characteristic $p$.

title: On integers $n$ relatively prime to $\lfloor αn^2\rfloor$
abstract: For $α\in\mathbb{R}$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S_{α,k}(x):=\#\{n\in\mathbb N:n\le x,\ \gcd(n,\lfloorαn^k\rfloor)=1\}$. Roth conjectured, and Watson proved, that $S_{α,1}(x)\sim 6x/π^2$ for every irrational $α$. Whether the same asymptotic holds for every fixed $k\ge2$ is a special case of a question of Bergelson and Richter, and was asked explicitly by Champagne. We answer this for $k=2$, with no Diophantine condition on $α$: for every irrational $α$, $S_{α,2}(x)\sim x/ζ(2)$ as $x\to\infty$. More precisely, for every fixed $A>0$ we obtain an error term $O_A(x/(\log q(x))^A)$, where $q(x)$ is the largest continued-fraction convergent denominator of $α$ not exceeding $x$. The proof sieves $S_{α,2}(x)$ over divisors, splitting at the parameter $R=q(x)^{1/8}$. Divisors larger than $R$ are handled by reducing the condition $d\mid\gcd(n,\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ to Möbius sums over arithmetic progressions and applying Zhan's uniform estimate for exponential sums twisted by $μ(n)$ over short intervals; divisors at most $R$ are handled instead through the Erdős-Turán inequality together with Weyl-type bounds for quadratic exponential sums of the form $\sum e(βn^2)$.

title: Almost sure exponential stabilization of linear stochastic systems driven by a general $α$-stable process via discrete-time state feedback
abstract:
Given an unstable linear scalar differential equation $dx(t)=θx(t)dt$, $θ>0$, we show that it can be almost surely exponentially stabilized by a discrete-time feedback control driven by a general $α$-stable process. More precisely, consider the stochastically controlled system $dx(t)=θx(t)dt+bx(\lfloor t/τ\rfloorτ)dZ(t)$,
  where $Z(t)$ is a general $α$-stable process with $α\in(1,2)$, and $\lfloor t/τ\rfloor$ denotes the integer part of $t/τ$. Unlike the extensively studied driven Brownian-driven case, the $α$-stable process has no finite second moment, so high-order moment methods are no longer applicable. By using fractional moments, characteristic functions, and moment inequalities for $α$-stable stochastic integrals, we prove that the stochastically controlled system is almost surely exponentially stable provided that the inequality $|bσ|^α\left(1-β\operatorname{sgn}(b)\tan^2\frac{πα}{2}\right)>(θ+bμ) \frac{-1}{Γ(α)\cos\frac{απ}{2}}$ holds, and that $τ>0$ is sufficiently small.

title: Optimal no-feedback card guessing after a fixed number of riffle shuffles
abstract: An ordered deck of $n$ cards is subjected to $k$ independent Gilbert--Shannon--Reeds riffle shuffles. A player then guesses each card without feedback, with repeated guesses allowed. For every fixed $k\ge1$, we prove that, once $n$ is sufficiently large, an optimal guess at position $i$ in the top half of the deck is $\lfloor i/2^k\rfloor+1$; the bottom-half strategy is obtained by reflection. We also show that the optimal expected number of correct guesses is $2\sqrt{n/((2^k-1)π)}+O_k(1)$. Our starting point is the result of our earlier work that the label at each position is distributed as an equally weighted mixture of $2^k$ components, each a shifted sum of two independent binomial random variables (a Poisson-binomial distribution). The proof of the optimal strategy combines three ingredients: a uniform concentration estimate that separates the mixture components, exact binomial inequalities that control the gaps between competing peaks, and a coefficient comparison that resolves modal ties. The expected-score asymptotic is proved independently of the strategy, using only the peak heights of the mixture components.

title: Reflective algebras over factorizable Hopf algebras
abstract: The reflective algebra $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$, introduced by Laugwitz, Walton and Yakimov, is a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra constructed from a quasitriangular Hopf algebra $(H,R)$ and a left $H$-comodule algebra $A$. We study the structure and factorizability of finite-dimensional reflective algebras. When $(H,R)$ is factorizable, we show that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is isomorphic, as a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra, to $A\otimes H$ equipped with the trivial left $H$-coaction on $A$ and the universal $K$-matrix induced by $R_{21}R$. In this case, we also classify all universal $K$-matrices on $R_H(A)$. Finally, we prove that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is factorizable if and only if $(H,R)$ is factorizable and $A$ is simple as an algebra.

title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties in Characteristic Zero
abstract: We construct a canonical projectivization of every smooth proper algebraic variety $X$ in characteristic zero. Once a principalization procedure is fixed, the construction gives a finite sequence of blowups in smooth centers with smooth projective endpoint, natural under semilinear isomorphisms and preserving the quasi-projective core, the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective open subsets. At each stage we select finitely many ideals near the generic points of the image in $X$ of the boundary of a maximal quasi-projective open. Principalizing their product strictly lowers the dimension of that image. The selection is defined intrinsically, without a polarization or a chosen projective modification; a Hilbert scheme argument proves its finiteness. Naturality embeds the automorphism group in that of a smooth projective variety of the same dimension. We then extend the construction to smooth proper integral algebraic spaces, obtaining canonical projectivizations of all compact connected Moishezon manifolds.

title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs under the Ore-type condition
abstract:
Stein conjectured that for every positive integer $k$, every oriented graph with minimum semi-degree greater than $k/2$ contains every oriented path of length $k$ [Springer Optim.Appl. 165 (2020), 459--486]. For directed paths this is a classical result of Jackson (1981). The two-block case of the conjecture was established by Chen, Hou and Zhou (2025). In this paper we prove the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem.
  For all positive integers $s$ and $r$, let $P(s,r)$ be the oriented path consisting of two directed paths of lengths $s$ and $r$ with a common terminal vertex, and let $Q(s,r)$ be its reverse. We show that for all $K\ge3$ and all $s,r\ge1$ with $s+r\le K$, every oriented graph $D$ with
  $δ(D)\ge K$ and $d_D^+(u)+d_D^-(v)\ge K-1$ for every ordered pair of distinct vertices
  $(u,v)\notin A(D)$ contains both $P(s,r)$ and $Q(s,r)$. Our result is the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem, and it extends the two-block result of Chen, Hou and Zhou. The proof iterates a shift of the terminal vertex of a longest path.

title: Online packing of the three largest trees
abstract:
For every $n\ge4$, arbitrary trees of orders $n,n-1,n-2$ can be packed into $K_n$ online, in decreasing order of size: each tree must be embedded before the next is revealed, and earlier embeddings cannot be changed. This strengthens the classical three-tree packing theorem of Hobbs, Bourgeois and Kasiraj (1987). In particular, the second tree is embedded without knowing the third, and the resulting pair of copies can be extended to accommodate every possible third tree.
  Our strategy is to embed the first two trees so that their union is $2$-degenerate. We prove that the complement of every $2$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices contains every tree of order $n-2$, which guarantees the final move. The main ingredient is an embedding lemma for spiders whose center must occupy a prescribed vertex having degree at most two in the forbidden graph. We then extend this lemma to arbitrary trees by induction.

title: Uniform boundary observability for periodic wave equations with low frequency exponent $4/3$
abstract: We study boundary observability for Dirichlet wave equations with symmetric, periodic coefficients in bounded $C^{2,1}$ domains of dimension $d\ge2$. We establish two-sided observability estimates, uniform in the oscillation scale $\varepsilon$, for initial data generated by eigenfunctions with eigenvalues at most $δ\varepsilon^{-4/3}$ with some small factor $δ$. The proof reduces wave observability to boundary gradient estimates for narrow spectral clusters. These estimates are obtained using a second-order expansion and a uniform commutator estimate for harmonic extension in boundary layers.

title: Effective results in representation theory of reductive groups over local fields
abstract: We prove effective versions of several classical results in representation theory of reductive groups over non-Archimedean local fields of arbitrary characteristic. More specifically, we deal with the support of matrix coefficients of cuspidal representations and the recursions satisfied by matrix coefficients of representations of finite length. We provide effective generation results for irreducible representations. Finally, we study the effective smoothness of characters on the set of regular semi-simple elements.

title: Derivation of a bending model for rods from finite viscoelasticity
